name: Ivo Carnotensis
evidence: Claim states 'All three major canonical collections remain in Latin' with '288 letters studied in academic publications but not translated into English.' Found: Individual letters (subset of the full 288) have been translated to English and are available on the Epistolae project at Columbia University (epistolae.ctl.columbia.edu). These English translations exist for correspondence with specific women in the Middle Ages, though the comprehensive canonical collections (Tripartita, Decretum, Panormia) remain untranslated.

name: Adamus Scotus (Adam of Dryburgh)
evidence: Claim states entire corpus untranslated, specifically 'De tripartito tabernaculo' and 'Liber de quadripartito exercitio cellae.' Found: 'Six Christmas Sermons' by Adam of Dryburgh was translated to English by M.J. Hamilton and published in 1974 in Analecta Cartusiana series (volume 16) by Institut für Englische Sprache und Literatur. Hamilton's translation was originally a Ph.D. thesis (Catholic University of America, 1964). De tripartito tabernaculo remains untranslated. Additionally, recent scholarship indicates an edition and translation of Soliloquium de instructione animae based on fifteen manuscripts was published in The Innes Review (2023).

name: Angelomus Luxovensis
evidence: Searched for 'Angelomus Luxovensis biblical commentary English', 'Angelomus Luxeuil Commentary Genesis', and checked Corpus Christianorum in Translation series and Dallas Medieval Texts. Academic sources reference his commentaries but only Latin editions are discussed. No English translation of Commentarius in Genesin, Enarrationes In Libros Regum, or Enarrationes In Cantica Canticorum found.

name: Othlonus S. Emmerammi Ratisponensis
evidence: Searched for 'Othlonus Emmeram theological writings', 'Otloh Saint-Emmeram'. Found that his works (Liber Visionum, Vitae Bonifatii, Libellus Proverbiorum, Dialogus de suis tentationibus) are available in Latin or German editions in MGH, but no English translations were found. Library of Congress holds manuscript collections of his writings, but editions appear to be Latin or German only.

name: Freculphus Lexovensis
evidence: Searched for 'Freculphus Historiarum libri XII English translation' and 'Freculphus universal chronicle.' Found that the Twelve Books of Histories is a major work in Latin (critical editions exist, including M.I. Allen ed., Brepols). Extensive medieval scholarship discusses the work but no English translation was located. Not listed in Dallas Medieval Texts or other major translation series.

name: Wolbero S. Pantaleonis
evidence: Searched for 'Wolbero Commentaria super Canticum Song of Songs English.' Found reference to the work in HathiTrust and AbeBooks Latin editions, but no English translation identified. Modern scholarship discusses his Commentary on Song of Songs but only in Latin or reference context.

name: Aimoinus Floriacensis
evidence: Searched for 'Aimoinus Floriacensis Historia Francorum English translation' and 'medieval chronicles translated Aimoinus.' Found Historia Francorum in Latin manuscripts and editions (Gallica, BnF), but no English translation located. Extensive academic references but only to Latin/French editions.

name: Hugo Rothomagensis
evidence: Searched for 'Hugo Rothomagensis medieval works English.' Limited sources found; no English translations identified. References to his work exist in medieval scholarship but primarily in Latin form.

name: Joannes Belethus
evidence: Searched for 'Joannes Belethus Summa ecclesiasticis officiis English translation.' Claim note correctly states 'German translation (Weinrich, CCT 11) but no English.' Corpus Christianorum in Translation series volume 11 contains German translation of 'Summe der kirchlichen Offizien' but NOT English. No English translation located in other sources. WorldCat and Brepols show only Latin critical edition.

name: Heterius Uxamensis
evidence: Searched for 'Heterius/Eterius Adversus Elipandum English translation.' The 'Adversus Elipandum libri duo' (co-authored with Beatus of Liebana) is available only in Latin critical editions (Corpus Christianorum, 1984 ed. by B. Löfstedt). No English translation found despite this being a significant anti-adoptionist work. Scholarly works discuss it in Latin or with European language apparatus.

name: Bandinus
evidence: Searched for 'Bandinus Peter Lombard Sentences commentary English.' Found manuscripts at Bodleian Library (MS. Bodl. 397, MS. Laud Misc. 477) and references to PL 192 Latin edition, but no English translation identified. Scholarly works on medieval Sentences commentaries discuss Bandinus only in Latin context.

name: Hildefonsus Toletanus
evidence: Claim states 'works on baptism and theological writings remain untranslated.' Found: 'Crown of the Virgin' (Libellus de Corona Virginis), one of Ildephonsus's major works, has been translated to English and published by TAN Books. This is described as meditations on the Blessed Virgin. Corpus Christianorum in Translation series lists Hildefonsus under 'Hagiografía visigótica' (in preparation, Spanish translation). The bulk of his other works may remain untranslated, but at least this Marian work is now available in English.

name: Folcuinus Laubiensis
evidence: Searched for 'Folcuin Lobbes Chronicle English translation.' Found extensive medieval scholarship on Folcuin of Lobbes (Gesta abbatum Lobiensium) in academic journals and books discussing his work, but only Latin editions and scholarly analyses were found. The chronicle remains untranslated into English.

name: Ammonius Alexandrinus
evidence: Searched for 'Ammonius Alexandrinus grammatical works English translation.' Found references to Latin editions (Ammonius De Differentia Adfinium Vocabulorum) and Byzantine scholarship, but no modern English translation of his grammatical works located. The work is available in archive.org in Latin form but not in English translation.

name: Ogerius Lucedii
evidence: Searched for 'Ogerius Lucedii Cistercian abbot sermons English.' Found references to Oglerius de Locedio (d. 1214) and his Tractatus in laudibus Sancte Dei Genitricis (13 sermons) and Sermones XV, preserved in PL 184 and Czech National Library, but no English translation located. Manuscripts are catalogued in Manuscriptorium but only in Latin.

name: Placidus Nonantulani
evidence: Searched for 'Placidus Nonantulani glossary medieval lexicon English.' Found references to Placidus's glossary as a classical Latin lexical work with textual history studied in academic sources, but no English translation identified. The work remains available primarily in Latin critical editions.

name: Braulio Caesaraugustanus
evidence: Claim states 'no English translation found.' FOUND: 'Iberian Fathers, Volume 2: Writings of Braulio of Saragossa and Fructuosus of Braga' translated by Claude W. Barlow, published by Catholic University of America Press (1969) as part of 'The Fathers of the Church: A New Translation' series (volume 63). This volume includes an extensive collection of letters from bishop Braulio of Saragossa, the Life of St. Emilian, and a list of the writings of Isidore—directly addressing the works cited in the claim.

name: Wicbodus
evidence: Searched for 'Wicbodus/Wigbod Quaestiones in Octateuchum English translation.' Found extensive academic references to Wigbod's 8th-century Genesis and Octateuch commentary prepared for Charlemagne, available in PL and scholarly editions, but no English translation publication located.

name: Luculentus
evidence: Searched for 'Luculentus homiliary homilies English translation.' Found that the Homiliary of Luculentius (156 homilies, early medieval Catalonia) has been studied in modern scholarship (research project preparing critical edition at UAB), but only 49 of 156 homilies have been published to date, and no English translation was located. The work remains in Latin.
